title: ringswim c1 on seed 4: swimming replicates (18 segments >= 3 BL, mu=0: 0), division is reticulate (labkit 1 persistent split, 130 merges in 151 splits); S, I, M supported, D not endorsed
summary: Fresh seed 4 of world_claim.py to t=20000. Walled cells condense from noise by t=800 and stay a bounded population of 9-18 round and bean-shaped cells with depletion wakes (rerun/sheet.png); late in the run several cells stretch into long crescents (t=17300-19200). c07's celltrack.py: 18 segments >= 3 BL, 2 >= 5 BL; 34 persistent splits, max generation 13, but 57 merges against 87 splits and 52 deaths. world_mu0.py on the same seed: 0 segments >= 3 BL, 34 persistent splits, 1 merge, max generation 4. labkit on the claim world (frames 100 t apart): 151 splits, 130 merges, 1 persistent split, max generation 1.

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: smoothed noise everywhere; cells by t=800
observations.I: rerun/sheet.png and rerun/tracks.png: 9-18 discrete walled cells through t=20000
observations.M: data/summary.txt: 18 celltrack segments >= 3 BL (2 >= 5 BL) vs 0 with mu=0 on the same seed

verdicts.limitation: D not endorsed: with the drive on, merges are 66% of splits on celltrack and 86% on labkit, which finds 1 persistent split; generation depth 13 by celltrack comes from a lineage that keeps fusing. The immotile mu=0 twin divides cleanly (34 persistent splits, 1 merge), so swimming brings collisions that undo divisions. I did not follow one cell that both divides and swims (the claim's track is on seed 1). Motion is slow and the drive is a per-body label average.
